title: Capture cleanup failure turns accepted checkpoints into errors and blocks every later checkpoint
opus_evidence: local-workspace-projection-operation.ts:1600-1602 (diff) calls removeLocalWorkspaceCheckpointCapture unguarded in finally, so a throw there replaces run's result or error; prepareLocalWorkspaceCheckpointCapture (local-workspace-checkpoint.ts:1170) and the unchanged-probe path (local-workspace-projection.ts:1669) remove the leftover first and rethrow, so an unremovable checkpoint-capture fails every later checkpoint. fs-safe-copy.worker.ts remove only retries once after chmod repair and otherwise throws.
gpt_evidence: The awaited cleanup in src/gateway/worker-environments/local-workspace-projection-operation.ts:115 is inside finally, so its rejection overrides either a successful acceptance or an error from the checkpoint. If the artifact remains unremovable, src/gateway/worker-environments/local-workspace-checkpoint.ts:55 retries removal before pausing, and src/gateway/worker-environments/local-workspace-projection.ts:150 retries it even on the unchanged path.
later_note: Accepted captures are now renamed and deleted in the background with failures only logged, so accepted checkpoints no longer turn into errors, but leftover retired captures are still removed unguarded before the next capture (bfe47f1ccbf8 later stops using snapshot capture for ordinary checkpoints).

title: Snapshots can delete canonical files backed by host mounts
opus_evidence: With capture set, local-workspace-manifest-scan.ts:1452-1454 scans the snapshot root and workspace-actual-manifest.ts only treats ino 2 directories as incomplete, with no mount or device check, so a host-namespace bind mount (invisible to a btrfs snapshot) scans as an empty ordinary directory and its accepted files read as deleted; this needs an operator to bind-mount on the host inside a private projection, since guest container mounts are not visible to the Gateway's live scan either.

The scanner records the unseen baseline file as a deletion at src/gateway/worker-environments/local-workspace-manifest-scan.ts:623, and src/gateway/worker-environments/workspace-reconcile-preflight.ts:194 selects that deletion for application when the canonical file still matches the baseline.
later_note: No commit listed for the manifest scan addresses bind-mounted directories missing from the btrfs snapshot.

title: Foreign-owned snapshot directories can block all later checkpoints
opus_evidence: fs-safe-copy.worker.ts prepareOwnedDirectoryRemoval skips chmod when (mode & 0o700) === 0o700 (a root-owned 0755 dir), so the second rmSync fails EACCES again for a non-root Gateway and the snapshot (which keeps guest ownership) stays; containers default to root (sandbox config user is optional, container-allocation.ts:106). This is a concrete trigger of the F1 cleanup failure that fails the accepted checkpoint and every later one.
gpt_evidence: A snapshot preserves the foreign UID on a populated 0755 directory, so an unprivileged Gateway without write access cannot unlink its children, and src/infra/fs-safe-copy.worker.ts:39 skips chmod because the owner bits already include 0700. The second removal attempt at src/infra/fs-safe-copy.worker.ts:137 fails and leaves the capture that subsequent checkpoints must remove at src/gateway/worker-environments/local-workspace-checkpoint.ts:55.
later_note: No listed fs-safe-copy worker commit changes the cleanup chmod/ownership handling for foreign-owned snapshot directories.

title: Native benchmark loses its report on a standard cgroup v2 host
opus_evidence: scripts/perf/local-workspace-checkpoint-measure.ts:2084-2086 enables accounting whenever /sys/fs/cgroup/cpu.stat exists, and :2285 then reads /sys/fs/cgroup/cpu.max unguarded; cgroup v2 root has cpu.stat but no cpu.max, so a run without a cgroup namespace throws ENOENT while building the report. The doc (local-workspace-checkpoint-measure.md:42-43) asks for an exclusively owned cgroup, so this is a misconfigured-rig case.
gpt_evidence: On a Linux cgroup v2 root that exposes cpu.stat, scripts/perf/local-workspace-checkpoint-measure.ts:2085 enables accounting. The unguarded cpu.max read at scripts/perf/local-workspace-checkpoint-measure.ts:2285 throws ENOENT because the root lacks that file, preventing the report write at scripts/perf/local-workspace-checkpoint-measure.ts:2373.
later_note: The benchmark report now reads /sys/fs/cgroup/cpu.max only if it exists and records null otherwise.
